commit.subject: [tint]: WIP: support texture-format-tier1
commit.message:
[tint]: WIP: support texture-format-tier1

Tint changes:
- Update core/texel_formats.def
- Update language specific def files:
  - Classify new texel formats as yielding f32, i32, u32 data
- Update language-specific printers
- WGSL resolver validation
- Update IR proto
- Update IR validation test for message change
- Update error message in unit test
- Update resource binding enums, and inspector mappings
- Generate skips for GLSL backend end2end tests

Dawn changes:
- Update resource binding mappings from Tint inspector

This needs additional changes in dawn/native/Format.cpp, which is
already in flight

Fixed: 421948908
Change-Id: Ibc18ac2a28d2439362ded9811e67282ca0c73f3e

parents.subject: [dawn][native] Make the device lock recursive for error handling.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Refactors the device-wide lock.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Refactors the device-wide lock.

- Makes the device lock much more similar to MutexProtected Guards.
- While guards are usually the one that expose the Defer function,
  we put the Defer function on the Device instead because unlike
  usual Guards that only live in the scope of a lambda, the new
  DeviceGuard acts much more like a lock.
- Use the guard everywhere instead of the lock so that we can
  use the Defer function where necessary in follow up changes.

Bug: 40643114, 42241400
Change-Id: I7d02fe3bbf9697b7539a959cc746c7cd163ce9da

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Refactors the device-wide lock.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Refactors the device-wide lock.

- Makes the device lock much more similar to MutexProtected Guards.
- While guards are usually the one that expose the Defer function,
  we put the Defer function on the Device instead because unlike
  usual Guards that only live in the scope of a lambda, the new
  DeviceGuard acts much more like a lock.
- Use the guard everywhere instead of the lock so that we can
  use the Defer function where necessary in follow up changes.

Bug: 40643114, 42241400
Change-Id: I7d02fe3bbf9697b7539a959cc746c7cd163ce9da

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Make a separate entry point for ExecutionQueue for callbacks.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Make a separate entry point for ExecutionQueue for callbacks.

- We have seen lock inversion issues w.r.t the lock in ExecutionQueue
  and the device lock before (see 417802523). In order to avoid this
  as the device-lock is a temporary solution for multithreading, this
  change introduces a separate function that we can use to implement
  new code without running into the lock ordering issue.
- This change also depends on the fact that the device lock is now
  recursively acquireable and makes all implementations (modulo Metal)
  explicitly acquire the device lock for CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials.
  We may be able to remove some of those locks, as we go forwards hence
  the TODOs.
- This change also allows us to revert the change in:
  https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/246534 so that we can
  guarantee callback ordering. For context, if we call the callbacks
  like we did before outside of the lock after moving them into a
  temporary vector, two threads updating serials 1 and 2 respectively
  can race and each remove one task, then in the non-critical section,
  serial 2's thread can run first resulting in what appears to be
  out of order callback execution. This design has some restrictions
  documented in the comments, but may be alleviated in the future if
  needed by using a recursive mutex for the waiting tasks in
  ExecutionQueue.

commit.message:
[tint][spir-v] Improve spir-v version robustness

Fix: 428041882

* The SPIR-V version enum is exposed via the options
* Improve the robustness of its usage by removing the specific values
    in the enum
* Add checks that only valid values can be used
* Move conversion to the version word into the printer
* Add validation environment settings to IRFuzzer validation

commit.subject: spirv-reader: spec op iadd, isub, imul
commit.message:
spirv-reader: spec op iadd, isub, imul

These binary WGSL operators require consistent types
for their arguments and result type.  But the SPIR-V operations
can have differing signedness for any of them.
Inject bitcasts as necessary to make them the same.

Fixed: 402726681 402726207 402726051
Change-Id: If0c9ba13bcfda7b15688b7c72f5a70c7aec8d3a5

commit.subject: Cache VkFramebuffers (reland)
commit.message:
Cache VkFramebuffers (reland)

Creation of VkFramebuffers is more expensive than expected on mobile
devices, so this introduces a framebuffer cache to reduce that
overhead.

Previous attempt at landing was reverted after crashes reported in
https://crbug.com/425093010, which seem limited to devices with Samsung
Xclipse GPUs (AMD-based).

For the sake of trying to keep this landed, changed the toggle logic to
opt-in and am only enabling it on ARM and Imagination GPUs, where it's
been observed to work correctly. Other GPUs can be allow-listed over
time once they have been verified or had bugs fixed.

Bug: 416088623
Change-Id: I3fcbf374d530ecc2be0db87ee70d781e1b249699

commit.subject: Cache VkFramebuffers (reland)
commit.message:
Cache VkFramebuffers (reland)

Creation of VkFramebuffers is more expensive than expected on mobile
devices, so this introduces a framebuffer cache to reduce that overhead.

Previous attempt at landing was reverted after crashes reported in
https://crbug.com/425093010, which seem limited to devices with Samsung
Xclipse GPUs (AMD-based).

Discovered that the likely reason for the crashes was that Vulkan may
re-use handle values for things like image views, making them
inappropriate for use as cache keys, as I was doing previously.
Refactored this CL to use explicit unique IDs instead, which resolved
the problems on the hardware I tested against.

Bug: 416088623
Change-Id: I3fcbf374d530ecc2be0db87ee70d781e1b249699

commit.subject: [tint][glsl] Support binding_array in texture_builtins_from_uniform
commit.message:
[tint][glsl] Support binding_array in texture_builtins_from_uniform

The options to texture_builtins_from_uniform are augmented to contain an
explicit offset and metadata count for each binding point (so that
binding_arrays can correspond to a span of the metadata passed by
uniform buffer). Multiple helpers are updated to pass the additional
options.

texture_builtins_from_uniform is changed to use get the "Path" for each
use of texture in the emulated builtins and uses that path to compute an
offset into the uniform buffer containing the metadata. Due to layout
restrictions, the uniform buffer cannot be a packed array<u32> so
instead it is an array<vec4> that needs two indexing operations to get
the u32 we require.

Tests are added.

Bug: 411573957
Change-Id: I699f72e78d23dce5cc8b8ce7e5096a7e025c29e5

This commit enables RENDER_ATTACHMENT, blendable, and multisampling support, as well as STORAGE_BINDING (read-only and write-only), for R16Unorm, R16Snorm, RG16Unorm, RG16Snorm, RGBA16Unorm, and RGBA16Snorm texture formats. These new capabilities are conditional on the texture-formats-tier1 feature being enabled.

Bug: 421941589

commit.subject: Handle `offset` in `subgroupMatrixStore` for `i8` `u8` matrices
commit.message:
Handle `offset` in `subgroupMatrixStore` for `i8` `u8` matrices

In WGSL the `offset` means the number of subgroup matrix elements, while
in SPIR-V the `offset` is applied to the output pointer. So when calling
`subgroupMatrixStore` to store an `i8` or `u8` subgroup matrix into an
`i32` or `u32` array, we need to divide 4 on the WGSL `offset` to match
the type of the SPIR-V output pointer.

Bug: 348702031, 403609083
Test: tint_unittests, dawn_end2end_tests
Change-Id: I4bc95caef59a0b5537d4c91a505128d0db89d0fe

commit.subject: [dawn] Fix nullability of WGPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor.bindGroupLayouts
commit.message:
[dawn] Fix nullability of WGPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor.bindGroupLayouts

The 'optional': true on this member was setting it WGPU_NULLABLE, which
is technically true, but we don't do this for any of the other array
members. The 'optional' here actually meant something very different,
that the *inner* object was nullable, not that the array was nullable.
So renamed that to 'array_element_optional'.

Bug: 427657664
Change-Id: I92bfb4f7694d472ddd1a1d7ebe31aada360d003e

commit.subject: [dawn] Add nullable support to return types
commit.message:
[dawn] Add nullable support to return types

Change return types to be more like RecordMember (type, annotation,
optional) rather than a raw Type. This requires a bunch of refactoring,
but now allows attaching that info to return types.

- Introduce a base class of RecordMember called AnnotatedTypedMember
  that only has type, annotation, optional, and json_data.
- Change the representation of function/method return types from a Type
  `.return_type` to an AnnotatedTypedMember `.returns`.
- Change the representation of void return to `None` instead of
  `types['void']`.
- Change the return type of CreateBuffer from "buffer" to
  {"type": "buffer", "optional": true}.

Bug: 427657664
Change-Id: Ifc3197139cdb3de5914c6bb33dd1b1c2dd20f1ce

commit.subject: Don't validate passes when validation is disabled
commit.message:
Don't validate passes when validation is disabled

Pass descriptors were still being validated even when validation was
disabled. In the case of Render passes the Skia team observed this
taking a non-trivial amount of time. This change skips pass validation

disabled. In the case of Render passes the Skia team observed this
taking a non-trivial amount of time. This change skips pass validation
for render and compute passes if validation has been disabled.

commit.subject: [tint][glsl] Handle binding_array in the unsampled case.
commit.message:
[tint][glsl] Handle binding_array in the unsampled case.

The computation of the replacement for texture bindings that are
unsampled is different than for the sampled case because depth_texture
needs to be turned into texture_2d<f32>. When adding support for
binding_array this code path wasn't handled, incorrectly transforming
the IR when a texture only had unsampled usages.

Adds a test for the unsampled usage of the binding_array textures to
fix missing coverage.

Bug: 411573957
Change-Id: Ie531cc83a0d056e82d57136289eac9392330676c

commit.subject: [spirv] Handle `offset` in `subgroupMatrixLoad` for `i8` `u8` matrices
commit.message:
[spirv] Handle `offset` in `subgroupMatrixLoad` for `i8` `u8` matrices

In WGSL the `offset` means the number of subgroup matrix elements, while
in SPIR-V the `offset` is applied to the input pointer. So when calling
`subgroupMatrixLoad` to load an `i8` or `u8` subgroup matrix from an
`i32` or `u32` array, we need to divide 4 on the WGSL `offset` to match
the type of the SPIR-V input pointer.

Bug: 348702031, 403609083
Test: tint_unittests
Change-Id: I52a2d89b6b041178e5a4e86e604d16ca2f3882cf

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Make buffer mapping thread-safe.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Make buffer mapping thread-safe.

- Introduces the Defer class and adds functionality of it to
  MutexProtected. This allows for use to queue additional work once
  a mutex is released. This is especially necessary for Buffers
  because it is common for users to re-entrantly call
  GetMappedRange in the MapAsync callbacks.
- Coalesces buffer mapping state and protects the state via
  MutexProtected.
- Updates |completedSerial| in QueueAndSerial to be atomic
  because spontaneous events may modify and read it concurrently.

Bug: 412761228, 418165343, 42241400, 40643114
Change-Id: If5ea22f81c6d305d1dee90eb3cf6276061e2f888

- Introduces the Defer class and adds functionality of it to
  MutexProtected. This allows for use to queue additional work once
  a mutex is released. This is especially necessary for Buffers
  because it is common for users to re-entrantly call
  GetMappedRange in the MapAsync callbacks.
- Renames GetMappedPointer->GetMappedPointerImpl for the frontend
  class, and then implements GetMappedPointer to take into account
  the staging buffer. This is more in line with how the rest of
  the Buffer's *Impl functions look and are handled. This also
  allows some cleanup of overly specialized code.
- Coalesces buffer mapping state and protects the state via
  MutexProtected.
- Updates |completedSerial| in QueueAndSerial to be atomic
  because spontaneous events may modify and read it concurrently.
- Removes device wide lock acquiring when calling GetMappedRange
  and its variants now that they are protected via the buffer
  lock.

Bug: 412761228, 418165343, 42241400, 40643114, 417802523
Change-Id: If5ea22f81c6d305d1dee90eb3cf6276061e2f888

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Updates buffer mapping w.r.t device lock.

The crux of this change is to make it such that users can
re-entrantly use *MappedRange functions and Unmap inside of
the MapAsync callback if the callback is successful. If the
callback was not successful, re-entrant API usage is not
allowed.

  class, and then implements GetMappedPointer to take into account
  the staging buffer. This is more in line with how the rest of
  the Buffer's *Impl functions look and are handled. This also
  allows some cleanup of overly specialized code.
- Coalesces buffer mapping state for clarity.
- Updates |completedSerial| in QueueAndSerial to be atomic
  because spontaneous events may modify and read it concurrently.
- Removes device wide lock acquiring when calling GetMappedRange
  and its variants now that we have an atomic to guarantee some
  code paths to be valid. This should increase performance on
  these buffers also.
- Refactors Unmap a bit to differentiate internal and external
  usages.
- Manually scope the device lock in Unmap to ensure that the
  callbacks are triggered in the right places.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Use a mutex for native event completion.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Use a mutex for native event completion.

- Without the new lock, there are occasional flakes in the
  new spontaneous BufferMapping tests because the test thread which
  calls |WaitAny(future, 0)| sometimes sees success and immediately
  starts tearing down the test, releasing the buffer, as the other
  thread actually tries to complete the callback.

Bug: 412761228
Change-Id: Idb74b3820bfafa0e1cca14d08ddd5c24f601ad18

parents.subject: [spirv] Support `i8` and `u8` in `subgroupMatrixMultiply{Accumulate}`

commit.subject: [spirv] Handle `stride` in `subgroupMatrixLoad` for `i8` `u8` subgroup matrices
commit.message:
[spirv] Handle `stride` in `subgroupMatrixLoad` for `i8` `u8` subgroup matrices

In WGSL the `stride` means the number of subgroup matrix elements, while in
SPIR-V the `stride` is related to the type of the input pointer. So when
calling `subgroupMatrixLoad` to load an `i8` or `u8` subgroup matrix from an
`i32` or `u32` array, we need to divide 4 on the WGSL `stride` to turn it into
the SPIR-V `stride`.

Bug: 348702031, 403609083
Change-Id: I045ae20d39351dbd6aaed50581730dc228f62485

commit.message:
ir-to-program: support bitcast in root block

Support override expressions with bitcasts.
This will be needed to support translating SPIR-V integer
operations with mixed-signedness arguments, but where WGSL
only supports same-signedness args.

commit.subject: [dawn] Make ComboLimits chain only standard limits extensions
commit.message:
[dawn] Make ComboLimits chain only standard limits extensions

ComboLimits always chains all limits structs. Tests use it for
requiredLimits, causing warning spam about some experimental limits
extensions (DawnTexelCopyBufferRowAlignmentLimits and
DawnHostMappedPointerLimits) which are currently output only - they're
ignored in requiredLimits, and operations are not validated against
them.

Remove those experimental limits extensions from ComboLimits. This also
obsoletes the #ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__ that I used previously to make this
work on Wasm.

Plus, revert "[dawn][wasm] Fixes WASM builds by excluding native utils."
2987f3c04d9b4f401dbe4fac6a52832ff90f17aa since this util should build in
Wasm targets now (both before and after this change).

Fixed: 416304914
Change-Id: I268a48180f30bddfbcc42955fc8682263fdaba7f

commit.subject: [dawn] Make ComboLimits chain only standard limits extensions by default
commit.message:
[dawn] Make ComboLimits chain only standard limits extensions by default

Some experimental limit extensions are currently output-only
(DawnTexelCopyBufferRowAlignmentLimits and DawnHostMappedPointerLimits
are ignored in requiredLimits, and operations are not validated against
them). Remove these experimental extensions from ComboLimits to stop
warning span about that problem. This also obsoletes the #ifdef
__EMSCRIPTEN__ that I used previously to make this work on Wasm.

Instead, callers can pass any additional extensions to GetLinked() as
variadic type-inferred arguments. Two tests are updated to use this.

Also revert 2987f3c04d9b4f401dbe4fac6a52832ff90f17aa
"[dawn][wasm] Fixes WASM builds by excluding native utils."
since that should no longer be necessary.

Fixed: 416304914
Change-Id: I268a48180f30bddfbcc42955fc8682263fdaba7f

Some experimental limit extensions are currently output-only
(DawnTexelCopyBufferRowAlignmentLimits and DawnHostMappedPointerLimits
are ignored in requiredLimits, and operations are not validated against
them). Remove these experimental extensions from ComboLimits to stop
warning span about that problem. This also obsoletes the #ifdef
__EMSCRIPTEN__ that I used previously to make this work on Wasm.

Instead, callers can pass any additional extensions to GetLinked() as
variadic type-inferred arguments. Two tests are updated to use this.

Also revert 2987f3c04d9b4f401dbe4fac6a52832ff90f17aa
"[dawn][wasm] Fixes WASM builds by excluding native utils."
since that should no longer be necessary.

entries but not reset `count_`. So, if you then called `IsEmpty` the map
would return false.

commit.message:

by its alignment, we need to add a @size() attribute to the previous
member.

commit.subject: d3d: Add missing unit test coverage of Compute2DTextureCopySplits to CopySplitTests
commit.message:
d3d: Add missing unit test coverage of Compute2DTextureCopySplits to CopySplitTests

This CL updates CopySplitTest::DoTest to emulate
RecordBufferTextureCopyWithBufferHandle in how it calls the Compute* and
Record* functions. Formerly, it handled 1D and 2D the same way, and
ignored 2D tests with more than 1 layer. Now, for 2D cases, it calls
Compute2DTextureCopySubresource (or
Compute2DTextureCopySubresourceWithRelaxedRowPitchAndOffset for
relaxed), and iterates over each layer, validating the computed values
per layer.

Bug: 424536624
Change-Id: Ibeeb047eb9ab216a7e689046b1a4b8af922c47b0

commit.subject: [tint][glsl] Move TextureBuiltinFromUniform after binding remapping.
commit.message:
[tint][glsl] Move TextureBuiltinFromUniform after binding remapping.

This is necessary to move it after DirectVariableAccess, which
simplifies the code of TextureBuiltinFromUniform and makes it easier to
add binding_array support in the future.

Concrete changes are:
 - Move TextureBuiltinFromUniform after DirectVariableAccess and after
   the BindingRemapper in GLSL's raise.cc.
 - Update the options of TexturnBuiltinFromUniform to use BindingInfo
   (for post-remaapping indices) instead of BindingPoint
   (pre-remapping), as well as places where this options are used
   (tests, GenerateBindings, CanGenerate).
 - Update ShaderModuleGL to produce post-remapping BindingInfo for
   TextureBuiltinFromUniform options.
 - Simplify TextureBuiltinFromUniform by removing the handling of
   function parameters now that it runs after DirectVariableAccess.
   (this logic was untested anyway).
 - Make the Tint inspector skip reporting ExternalTexture as needing
   metadata for textureDimensions as the dimensions come from the
   ExternalTexture UBO already.
 - Update tests for the GLSL output changes caused by the reordering of
   the transforms.

Bug: 411460085
Change-Id: Ica12f6140bf88c2ba858721986a8d9fdbf48461f

textures in the same bind group needing builtins from uniform.

We need to make sure these metadata are pushed to different offsets
and retrieved correctly in the shader.

commit.message:
[tint][fuzz] Use printer capabilities in writer_fuzz passes

Exposes the capabilites that are required after running all of the
transforms before the printer, and use them in the appropriate
writer_fuzz pass. This prevents spurious ICEs in the fuzzer due to IR
not being considered valid after running the transforms due to missing
capabilities.

commit.subject: [tint][glsl] Support binding_array in texture_polyfill
commit.message:
[tint][glsl] Support binding_array in texture_polyfill

Replaces the concept of finding the root variable for a given
texture/sampler value with the "path" which is a combination of a
variable and optionally an index to access that variable with.

Adds unittests for various kinds of paths for a texture value coming
from a binding array as well as tests showing that the whole
binding_array is duplicated in the bindings when used by multiple
samplers.

Bug: 411573957
Change-Id: I7cc718c03eeb410c84b0cdc180092543ccc81634

Original change's description:
> Revert "[dawn][metal] Makes AllowSpontaneous work for Metal queue events."
>
> This reverts commit b1c66af72925e24732b7c0f7c7275714d960b842.
>
> Reason for revert: Failures on Intel and AMD Macs, e.g.:
> https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Dawn%20Mac%20x64%20DEPS%20Release%20%28AMD%29
>
> Bug: 412761367
> Original change's description:
> > [dawn][metal] Makes AllowSpontaneous work for Metal queue events.
> >
> > - Since the queues in Metal are updated via Metal callbacks already,
> >   we can make AllowSpontaneous work by having the Metal callbacks
> >   directly call the queue callbacks as well.
> > - Adds spontaneous tests for queue events in Metal.

commit.subject: Reland "[dawn][metal] Makes AllowSpontaneous work for Metal queue events."
commit.message:
Reland "[dawn][metal] Makes AllowSpontaneous work for Metal queue events."

Relanding now that:
  - *MappedRange functions no longer acquire the device-wide lock.
  - The |completedSerial| in QueueAndSerial is atomic.

Previously, the issues above along with some lock scopes resulted in
deadlocks when spontaneous map async callbacks fired.

commit.subject: Reduce allocations in BindGroupTracker
commit.message:
Reduce allocations in BindGroupTracker

Profiling showed that the resize done on
mDynamicOffsets was causing allocations at an
inopportune time when submitting command buffers.

Attempts to resolve that by using a static array
with the maximum number of dynamic offsets and
tracking the count separately.

Bug: 424506429
Change-Id: Ic0b6a57e55e369413599bf453943e7d2b0748373

messages before running the printer.

commit.subject: [spirv-reader] Add support for Coherent decoration
commit.message:
[spirv-reader] Add support for Coherent decoration

Adds support for the decoration in the SPIR-V reader. As Tint's IR has
coherent semantics by default, this is a no-op in the parser.

Change-Id: I416a0c6d623f146cd88c71b15abe5d3bf583ad79
